Pascoe, of N.L.H., ran well in beating Fred White in the 880 Yards with a newcomer in Sergt.

The finish saw Herbert in front clocking 42.42; Hoath 2nd, 42.49; Carter 4th, 43.3; Tobin 15th, 44.44; Bryan 17th, 44.49; Cohen 18th, 45.4; Peck 21st, 45.15; Shields 25th, 45.34; Morrell 40th, 47.16; Spencer 55th, 49.25; White 63rd, 50.39 and Jannaway 70th, 53.30.
David Main won the One Mile Handicap off 125 yards in 4.20. White City (Whit Monday). Len Herbert was beaten by the New Zealander, Johnson, in 9m. 34s.

Putting the Shot (Junior Weight): 1 Smith (S.L.H.), 34 ft. 4ins.; 2 Bishop (B.), 30 ft. 11¾ ins.; 3 Machell (B.), 27 ft. 6ins. Javelin: 1 White (S.L.H.) (Junior Javelin), 153 ft. 10 ins.; 2 Powell (B.) (Senior Javelin), 126 ft. 10 ins.
Sid Ring was 5th in 2.6.15 and Fred White completed the team in 8th position in 2.7.38. Doubleday was 11th in 2.9.24 and Dick Towndrow was 15th in 2.11.26.
Dan Patience ran well to finish eighth, White and Doubleday, short of training, faded out over the last two miles and were both outside standard time (2.15).
White took Woodford into a lead here which they kept to the end, while Bert Ingles drew away from Alan to increase the Valley's lead over us to 29s.

When the Pompey runner moved away it seemed Chas. was to have one of those days , but when Haith (T.V.H.)and later White (Woodford) caught up it seemed to act as a tonic and he stayed with them to the end, where with a typical final flourish he kept us in third place, only thirty secs. down on Pompey.
Iron rallied strongly, Mac faded slightly, George Knight got cracking, and to rub salt into the wounds, White (Woodford) and Harper (Deptford) passed Mal on the run in.

The standard of competition was particularly high, especially in the sprints where Hercules Wimbledon's 16 year-old Martin Giraud ran 10.8 and Herne Hill's White clocked a 21.8 - not bad for a mid-week league!
